correctness.rationale: The claim is finite and exhaustible. The verifier constructs exactly all \(3^6=729\) words of the standard cyclic \([11,6,5]_3\) code, computes every cyclic \(b\)-window weight directly, independently recomputes it from cyclic zero-gap lengths, checks equality word-by-word for all \(1\le b\le11\), and reproduces both the published ordinary Hamming enumerator and published minimum \(b\)-distance hierarchy. The proof uses only the explicit generator polynomial and the elementary zero-gap counting identity.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2026 Golay paper proves the minimum \(b\)-distance hierarchy and minimum-support orbit facts but does not give complete \(b=2,3,4,5\) coefficient distributions. The related generalized-repetition example also gives only the distance hierarchy. The 2021 geometric theorem implies stabilization for \(b\ge6\), not the four nonstable spectra. Nearby complete-distribution work treats special irreducible cyclic-code families rather than supplying these Golay coefficients. Exact-coefficient and alias searches returned no covering result.

value.rationale: Complete \(b\)-symbol weight distributions are natural invariants for read-channel coding and strictly strengthen minimum \(b\)-distance data. The ternary Golay code is a canonical benchmark, and the four nonstable spectra quantify all codeword multiplicities rather than a chosen parameter slice. They can be used directly in exact finite performance calculations and as test data for general b-symbol enumerator identities; the result is not a mere recomputation of a known table.
